**Analysis of visual features:**

- **Affected part**: Leaf (appears to be tomato)
- **Leaf condition**: Very pronounced rolling/curling of the leaf — distorted and cupped
- **Lesions**: Numerous dark brown to black necrotic spots distributed across the leaf surface; spots appear to have somewhat irregular, blurred margins rather than sharply angular edges
- **Pattern**: Many spots coalescing in places; the leaf is heavily covered with lesions, contributing to browning and rolling

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Has small angular (straight-edged) spots with yellow halos and can cause leaf curling — but speck lesions are typically very small (1/16 in.), more pinpoint, and more sharply defined
- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus (TSWV)**: "Infected foliage may become covered with so many spots that leaves brown, roll, and wilt" — the leaf rolling is very pronounced here; "distinct necrotic spots, downward-cupped leaves"; TSWV lesions characteristically have **blurred margins**, which fits the irregular spot edges seen; this also fits the pattern of heavy spotting leading to leaf distortion
- **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus**: Causes mosaic patterns and shoestring leaves, not dark necrotic spots
- **Late Blight**: Would show water-soaked brown patches with pale halos, not discrete dark spots

The combination of prominent leaf rolling/curling with widespread dark necrotic spots having blurred margins most closely aligns with **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**.
